Subject: GDPR DPA & SCC module selection - follow-up from today's call

Hi John / ACME team,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we all stay aligned: 

1) DPA request: ACME asked for a copy of our standard DPA for review. I've attached a DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf) — it's our standard template and includes the SCCs we typically propose.

2) SCC module selection: Based on your data flows described on the call (customer data stored in US, analytics processing in EU, and cross-border transfers to US infra), we recommended Module 2 (Controller to Processor) plus the cross-border transfer clauses. I've attached an SCC module recommendation matrix for your team to review.

3) Roles: We discussed controller vs processor alignment. For the use case you outlined (ACME drives end-user selection and Redwood provides hosted inference), ACME is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. Please confirm if any contract language should treat ACME as joint controller for specific features.

4) SOC 2 / security posture: Rishi will share our SOC 2 timeline. High level: Type II in progress, expected completion Q4 2026; summary evidence can be shared under NDA sooner if helpful.

5) Next steps / owners: 
- Marissa: update DPA with any ACME redlines and share updated version (due: 2026-07-12).
- John / ACME: confirm controller/processor position and any special clauses (due: 2026-07-14).
- Rishi: share SOC 2 timeline and redacted control summaries (by 2026-07-10).
- Neha: start PSG / vendor security questionnaire intake if you want a centralized tracker.

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf (DPA template)
Attachment: SCC_module_recommendation_matrix.xlsx

I'll be around if you want to hop on a quick follow-up call.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary and the attachments — very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side after an initial pass: 

- Controller/Processor: confirmed — ACME will be Controller for core product usage. One exception: for the new analytics feature we may need to discuss whether Redwood acts as a sub-processor processing pseudonymized telemetry. We'll flag specific endpoints.

- SCC modules: the security team prefers the explicit Controller-to-Processor wording (Module 2). Can you confirm whether your DPA references the new EU SCCs (the 2021/2022 standard) or the older set? We need to ensure compatibility with our legal templates.

- SOC 2: request Rishi to share any interim reports or control mapping documents; NDA available on request.

We'll aim to get initial redlines by 2026-07-14. If anything else comes up we'll circle back earlier.

Best,

Following up on SOC 2 and SCC questions:
